item.title: When the Chips Are Down
item.description: President Trump’s reversal of a ban on sales of advanced semiconductors to China undercut the strategic logic behind years of American policy that was meant to keep the US ahead in the race to develop AI systems.

item.title: Toni Plays the Dozens
item.description: What’s so funny about Toni Morrison?

item.title: Mother Trouble
item.description: In her new memoir, Arundhati Roy tries to find the language to grapple with the shadow of her formidable, extraordinary mother.

item.title: Painted Sermons
item.description: The dazzling works of Fra Angelico both testify to the immense wealth and power of fourteenth-century Florentine society and attempt to heal its pride, greed, and brutal inequality.

item.title: American Imperialism and the End of Sovereignty
item.description: Fintan O’Toole hosts New York Review contributors Alma Guillermoprieto and Michael Ignatieff for a wide-ranging conversation on the Trump administration’s imperial ambitions in Venezuela, Greenland, and beyond. This conversation originally aired on February 5, 2026.

item.title: Darryl Pinckney on Memoir, Friendship, and Elizabeth Hardwick
item.description: In the first episode of our podcast Private Life, Darryl Pinckney talks with host Jarrett Earnest about his close friend and former teacher Elizabeth Hardwick.
